subject: UAE Open Finance: pay-by-bank fees are 38 bps, capped at AED 50
description: Pay-by-bank fees at 38 bps, capped at AED 50, and October's 842,969 API calls. What's new in UAE Open Finance since 29 October.
body:
Hello, and welcome to the second issue of the Open Finance OS briefing.

From this issue on we'll write every week, aligned with each new post, pulling together what's happened in UAE Open Finance, plus a few things from further afield worth knowing about. It's a community project, so if something's useful (or missing), hit reply and tell us.

Since we last wrote

Pay by Bank UAE Fees: 38 bps, Capped at AED 50, vs Cards
The AlTareq Commercial and Pricing Model caps the fee a TPP pays the payer's bank for a merchant collection at 38 basis points in Year 1, with a maximum of AED 50 per payment. The first AED 200 a TPP collects per merchant per day is exempt if the Merchant ID is in the request, and a person-to-person or SME-to-SME transfer is capped at 25 fils. These are caps, not list prices, and the public logs still can't tell us what October's AED 124.8 million in accepted payments earned anyone.

842,969 Calls: UAE Open Finance Doubled in October
October was the first month UAE Open Finance cleared 800,000 API calls. The public logs show 842,969 calls, up from 405,147 in September, a rise of 108.1%. Accepted payments in October were worth AED 124.8 million, and 95.7% of payments were accepted across the 12 full months.

18.4% API Errors: What UAE Open Finance Data Tells Builders
On 3 November we unpacked a figure that looks worse than it is: 18.4% of API calls returned an error across the 11 full months to September, even as 95.3% of payments were accepted. An error is not an outage — many are ordinary 4xx responses — and the two figures measure different things. Once October was a complete month, the cumulative error rate fell to 12.7%, largely because October added a lot of volume at a lower error rate.

UAE Open Finance V2.2: Due by Year-End, Still Not Final
Tier-1 banks and insurers must release V2.2 of the UAE Open Finance Standards into production by 31 December 2026, but the standard still isn't final: the current text is release candidate v2.2-rc2, and its publication date is TBC. In the 1 November production directory, none of the 51 API resource declarations was on v2.2.

Saudi Open Banking vs UAE Open Finance: Licences First, Hub First
Saudi Arabia and the UAE are both building regulated open banking in 2026, and they are doing it in almost opposite ways. SAMA licenses providers on a shared standard — four account-information licences announced that we could find, and no announced payment-initiation licence as of 12 November — while every UAE call runs through a single API Hub. The two markets also publish different numbers (connected accounts versus API calls and payments), so the post compares the models and does not rank one against the other.

We also published two weekly digests in this period: 26 Oct–2 Nov and 2–9 Nov. The registry changes they recorded are brought up to date in the Watch note below.

Ecosystem Watch

The latest Ecosystem Watch run is 16 November (API logs through 10 November). Compared with the 26 October run — the one nearest our first issue — here is what actually changed. Full-month traffic figures now include October, as in the post above; 1–10 November is still a partial month and is not a trend.

Production and sandbox. In the production directory, registrations rose from 30 on 29 October to 31 as of 15 November, after Al Ain Ahlia Insurance joined on 4 November. 14 of 31 registrations now publish an active authorization server, up from 13 of 30 on 29 October. On 3 November, Standard Chartered added BDSP and BSIP roles. ADCB added an Active ATM v2.1 resource; three production registrations now declare the ATM family, up from two. The 16 November directory read still finds no production API resource on v2.2. Sandbox registrations rose from 79 to 81: Network International joined on 9 November, and Ashii Finance Holding Limited on 11 November.

Specs and repos. The published standard is still v2.1-final, with errata 3, and the API Hub is still v8. There is still no v2.2 rc3 or final. The v2.2-rc2 changelog now lists 21 new rc2 entries plus 4 carried from rc1 (the 16 November watch notes that sections 18–21 were added on 4 November). The website spec branch remains v2.2-rc2-nebras; its head moved to 2b966abe on 4 November, and 18 tracked v2.2 spec files on that branch changed. The api-specs main branch is unchanged. community-standards and the Postman repo both have newer heads (12 November and 11 November). A 2 November confluence check also picked up the Limitation of Liability Model moving from v21 to v23 (dated 28 October).

Entities. The 16 November run confirmed uae-scretail as Standard Chartered Bank (Retail), a Tier-2 bank, and mapped Alain Ahlia Insurance to its production-directory organisation. Standard Chartered appears in the November API logs from 3 November, but the full-month live counts stay at 16 LFIs and 17 TPPs because November is still a partial month.

That's it for this issue

Thanks for reading issue 2. If you have news, data or a correction, just reply to this email. And if a colleague would find this useful, please forward it or point them to openfinance-os.org/newsletter.

Want to talk it through? Join the Open Finance OS community on Slack, where we'll share each issue and start a discussion.

See you next week,
Michael

subject: UAE Open Finance: why 12 of 30 registrations publish an auth server
body:
Hello, and welcome to the first issue of the Open Finance OS weekly briefing.

Each week we'll pull together what's happening in UAE Open Finance, plus a few things from further afield worth knowing about. It's a community project, so if something's useful (or missing), hit reply and tell us.

This week in UAE Open Finance

12 of 30: Why most UAE Open Finance registrations don't publish an authorization server
Only 12 of 30 production directory registrations publish an active authorization server, but that isn't a sign that 60% of the ecosystem is broken. In the UAE's centralised model, the Nebras-operated API Hub acts as the authorization server and consent store, and TPPs never call banks directly.

This week in UAE Open Finance: 19 to 26 October
Three registry changes: Zurich joined the production registry as an LFI, and EIB joined and added an LFI role. Al Tareq platform logs show 1,416,887 cumulative API calls from November 2025 to September 2026, with a 95.3% payment success rate.

Open finance arrives on the NBF Direct app with multi-bank access
National Bank of Fujairah began rolling out open finance in its NBF Direct app in September 2026, letting customers share their account data and do more in the app themselves.

Why open banking needs a sustainable commercial model to scale payments and AI services
At Sibos 2026, NatWest's Simon Eacott made the case that commercial models, A2A payments and AI are what take open banking to the next level. A useful lens for the UAE as usage grows.

Zen.com and Mastercard expand Pay by Bank across Europe
Zen.com now supports Pay by Bank through Mastercard Open Finance for merchant payments and wallet top-ups across nine European markets.

Agents and open finance

How would an AI agent actually reach your bank account in the UAE? Here's the simplified path: the customer consents, a licensed TPP (or the agent it runs) makes the request, and the Nebras API Hub sits between it and the bank.

Visa, BILL and Billtrust launch a live pilot for AI agent payments (Visa, 20 October)
AI agents registered through Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol are now paying approved supplier invoices end to end, using tokenised credentials instead of shared portal logins. It's an early real-world test of how an agent proves who it is and what it's allowed to do.

Mastercard opens Agent Pay for Machines to developers (Mastercard, October)
Businesses give an agent a spending limit, and the agent pays for services with signed vouchers that providers verify now and settle later. Early access APIs and a sandbox are open; no general availability date yet.

That's it for this week

Thanks for reading the first issue. If you have news, data or a correction, just reply to this email. And if a colleague would find this useful, please forward it or point them to openfinance-os.org/newsletter.

Want to talk it through? Join the Open Finance OS community on Slack, where we'll share each issue and start a discussion every week.

See you next week,
Michael
